key_insight: DermDepth shows that single-image, metric-scale 3D skin reconstruction is possible for dermatology, enabling more accurate lesion and wound measurement from standard cameras.
clinical_relevance: This could improve size tracking, morphology assessment, and monitoring across skin cancer screening and wound care without requiring extra hardware.
method: Trained a monocular 3D model for dermoscopic and macroscopic skin images
Created D-Synth, a synthetic dermoscopic dataset with pixel-perfect 3D labels
Fine-tuned on a small set of real clinical images to improve real-world generalization
evidence_signal: Training on D-Synth reduced metric scale error on real dermoscopic data from over 16x to under 1.1x, and the method was evaluated on three real-world benchmarks spanning millimeters to centimeters.
watch_item: Performance depends on synthetic-to-real transfer and limited real clinical fine-tuning, so broader validation is needed before routine deployment.
paper_title: DermDepth: Toward Monocular Metric Scale 3D Reconstruction Models for Dermatology
